issues.text: Fill answer set accepts singular and plural for subtype/subclass but only plural for the 'derived' forms, and has no Vietnamese 'dẫn xuất' form (the usual VN term for derived class). A learner typing 'derived class' or 'lớp dẫn xuất' is marked wrong for a correct answer.
issues.fix: Add "derived type", "derived class", "lớp dẫn xuất", "kiểu dẫn xuất" to `answer` of q6. No other change.

issues.text: Round 1 overlap is smaller but not gone: bullet 1 now corrects with 'keeping the promise for every input', yet its last sentence ('a new subtype compiles cleanly but callers ... start failing') is the point bullet 2 makes next. Reading bullet 2 felt like a repeat of bullet 1's ending.
issues.fix: End bullet 1 with a sign that is not about compiling, e.g. 'You notice this when a subtype that implements every method still makes callers fail for some inputs.' Leave bullet 2 as is.
issues.quote: You notice this when a new subtype compiles cleanly but callers that never changed start failing.

issues.text: Core concepts teaches 'subtype', but section 6 and quiz q2 switch to 'subclass'. I know 'derives from', so I guessed they mean the same thing, but for a moment I wondered whether a subclass is something different from a subtype.
issues.fix: Use 'subtype' in both section 6 bullets and in q2 (statement, options a and b), matching Core concepts.
issues.quote: As long as a subclass compiles against its base type, it automatically satisfies LSP.

issues.text: q4's explanation for b uses 'a narrower type', an idea the lesson never mentions, and the d explanation opens with a clause ('Another total would matter when you want one more value checked') I had to re-read to understand. Both explanations confused me more than the wrong option did.
issues.fix: b: 'The array is typed ShippingFee[], so any subtype can go in it and the test does pass.' d: 'At 1,000,000 the test would fail, which exposes the problem; one more value still would not prove every total.'
issues.quote: This would hold when the array had a narrower type, but it is `ShippingFee[]`, so any subtype fits and the test does pass.

issues.text: In q2, option c is clearly the longest and restates the lesson's wording ('parameters and return types', 'keeps its promise for every input'), while d is obviously false. I could pick c from length and familiar phrasing without thinking much.
issues.fix: Shorten c to about the length of a and b, e.g. 'False, because compiling does not check what the method does for each total.'
issues.quote: False, because compiling checks parameters and return types, not whether the method keeps its promise for every input.
